mechanism: Build continuous synthetic USD and EUR currency-strength indices as weighted geometric means of FX basket rates: USDX=50.14348112·EURUSD^(-0.576)·USDJPY^(0.136)·GBPUSD^(-0.119)·USDCAD^(0.091)·USDSEK^(0.042)·USDCHF^(0.036); EURX=34.38805726·EURUSD^(0.3155)·EURGBP^(0.3056)·EURJPY^(0.1891)·EURCHF^(0.1113)·EURSEK^(0.0785). Per M1 bar compute Open/High/Low/Close of the index by applying the same product to each OHLC of every basket symbol; tick_volume summed across basket.
data_needed: Live/history OHLC+ticks of basket FX pairs; SymbolWeight[] (symbol,weight); MAIN_COEFF; CustomRatesReplace / tick feed into a custom symbol.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDX basket: EURUSD,USDJPY,GBPUSD,USDCAD,USDSEK,USDCHF; EURX basket: EURUSD,EURGBP,EURJPY,EURCHF,EURSEK; M1 history (~1 month) then tick updates; custom symbol chart PERIOD_M1

mechanism: When synthesizing index M1 bars, each basket symbol keeps an index into its rates[]; if a minute has no bar for a symbol, reuse prior Close for Open/High/Low/Close contributions and only accumulate tick_volume when a symbol actually has a bar at that minute—if total tick_volume==0 skip the minute. Synchronize start_date to the latest first-bar time across the basket so all series share a common timeline.
data_needed: Per-symbol M1 MqlRates arrays; str_rates.index cursors; shared minute timeline.
why_new_for_mis: Turns sparse multi-symbol liquidity/gaps into an explicit alignment rule for basket sensors so MIS index bars reflect when the basket actually traded, not interpolated ghosts.

mechanism: Normalize open series to start at 1; define spread = open_usa − open_japan. Interpret spread>0 as US bonds outperforming JP bonds (and conversely); overlay vs USDJPY open to visually/test whether FX equilibrium shifts with relative bond performance—article notes the naive expectation does not always hold.
data_needed: Normalized opens of UST10Y and JGB10Y; USDJPY open; optional spread time series.

mechanism: Cross-validate 9 regressors under three feature sets: (1) USDJPY OHLCV only, (2) both bonds' OHLCV only, (3) union. Lowest validation RMSE was set (1); bonds-only worst; union better than bonds-alone but not better than FX-only. Tuned LinearSVR on full feature set still beats LinearRegression on held-out folds.
data_needed: Three predictor column groups; TimeSeriesSplit(n_splits=5,gap=20); MSE tables.
why_new_for_mis: Warns MIS that raw sovereign OHLCV can be strongly correlated yet add little (or hurt) vs FX tape for short-horizon USDJPY level prediction—ablation is itself a sensing-design result.

mechanism: Export tuned LinearSVR to ONNX; each tick standardize 15 inputs (2×bond OHLCV+vol + USDJPY OHLCV+vol), OnnxRun → forecast close. prediction=1 if forecast>spot else 2; enter Buy/Sell when flat; if state≠prediction close USDJPY (model-implied reversal).
data_needed: ONNX LSVR; per-column mean/std CSV; live iOpen/iHigh/iLow/iClose/iTickVolume for three symbols.

mechanism: On new bar, CopyHigh/CopyLow of last two closed bars; if high[0]<high[1] && low[0]>low[1] (inside bar), treat parent bar range as compression. Place BuyStop at high[1]+pips and SellStop at low[1]−pips; SL at mid-range (0.5·range), TP at 0.875·range beyond entry side; orders expire after N bars.
data_needed: Two closed bars High/Low; Point(); min lot; pending OrderSend fields.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any FOREX Symbol(), PERIOD_CURRENT (works even on M1; spread-dependent)
why_new_for_mis: Encodes a concrete range-compression→breakout sensor (inside-bar ⊆ parent) MIS can poll as a volatility-regime flag before breakout.
quote: an inside bar is a candlestick whose high and low are completely within the range of the previous (larger) candle.

mechanism: On new bar, CopyRates+CopyBuffer(iMA) for two closed bars. Buy regime if close[0]>ma[0] && ma[0]>ma[1]; sell if close[0]<ma[0] && ma[0]<ma[1]. One position per symbol; opposite signal closes then reverses; SL at signal bar low (buys) or high (sells).
why_new_for_mis: Pairs close-vs-MA side with MA slope into a single aligned trend-regime sensor used as both entry and reverse-exit gate.
